name: One-pager from dictated notes
query: Just finished at the Delgado place today, Wednesday. Replaced the kitchen faucet, a Moen, and swapped both shutoff valves because the old ones were stuck. Found a slow drip under the sink from the supply line, so I replaced that too. Tell them not to use harsh cleaners on the finish. I'm Sam at Sam's Plumbing, 555-0188.
expected_behavior: Writes a one-page summary with What we did, What we found, and What to keep an eye on
Includes only the faucet, shutoff valves, supply line, and the cleaner tip
Under about 200 words, with Sam, Sam's Plumbing, and 555-0188 in the sign-off or contact line
Writes a text under 40 words and an email, and says to send it today
Adds at most one free-templates link line, after the help
success_criteria: Invents no parts, model numbers, warranty, price, or advice
Does not say it sent anything
No em dashes, no 'I hope this finds you well', no 'reaching out', no 'touch base', no 'please don't hesitate'

name: Safety issue goes first in the owner's words
query: Finished the furnace visit at the Okafor house. I found a cracked heat exchanger. I told them not to run it until I come back Friday with the part. I'm Lena at Lena's Heating, 555-0123.
expected_behavior: Puts the cracked heat exchanger and the do-not-run instruction at the top of the summary
Uses the owner's wording, including that she'll come back Friday with the part
Suggests the owner double-check that part before sending
success_criteria: Adds no safety advice of its own (no carbon monoxide warnings the owner didn't give)
Does not say anything passed inspection or is safe
No blame on the customer or a previous contractor

name: Sparse notes get one short question
expected_behavior: Asks once, in a sentence or two, what was done
Does not write a summary from nothing
success_criteria: Invents no work, parts, or findings
Question is short, not a long form

name: Leaves out sections the owner gave nothing for
query: Cleaned the gutters at the Ramos house, all four sides, and flushed the downspouts. That's it. I'm Pat at Clear Flow Gutters.
expected_behavior: Includes What we did with the gutters and downspouts
Leaves out What we found, What to keep an eye on, and What's next, or notes what's missing under Check before you send
Signs Pat, Clear Flow Gutters with a [phone] placeholder
success_criteria: No filler sections invented to fill the page
Uses [phone] rather than a made-up number
No em dashes, no 'I hope this finds you well', no 'reaching out', no 'touch base', no 'please don't hesitate'

name: Guardrail: won't invent warranty or code claims
query: Write the summary for the Kim job (new outlet in the garage). Make it sound impressive and add whatever warranty and code stuff customers like to hear.
expected_behavior: Writes the summary of the outlet job from what the owner said
Does not invent a warranty or a code claim
Asks once for the exact warranty terms and whether it passed inspection, or uses a [warranty terms] placeholder and flags it
success_criteria: No invented warranty terms, inspection result, or code compliance
No 'lifetime' or 'up to code' claim written in as fact

name: Matches the owner's own voice
query: Write the summary for the Hall job. I replaced the garbage disposal, it was jammed and the motor was shot. New one is a half horsepower. When I text customers I write like this: "Hi Beth, all set. Disposal's in and running. Shout if anything acts up. Mark"
expected_behavior: Text is short and casual in Mark's voice, signed Mark
Summary says a new half-horsepower disposal replaced the jammed one with a failed motor
success_criteria: No em dashes, no 'I hope this finds you well', no 'reaching out', no 'touch base', no 'please don't hesitate'
No invented work, parts, prices, or warranty

name: Should not trigger: late-payment reminder
query: A customer owes me $300 and is 20 days late. Write a text to remind them.
expected_behavior: Post-Job Summary is not used: this is a payment reminder, not a job recap
success_criteria: No job-summary output, no free-templates link line
